renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: pair_flow_sankey
  title: Fate of the read pairs
  description: |-
    Each band is a group of read pairs flowing from how they mapped, through the restriction-fragment filter, to the contact class they end in. It answers where the sequenced pairs are lost on the way to valid contacts.
    How to read: a thick band into Lost at an early step is the main source of loss. A large dangling end or religation band points to a problem in the digestion or ligation, and a thin valid pairs band means most of the sequencing did not yield contacts. Compare samples through the table tile.
    Lines and annotations: dangling ends are unligated fragments with both reads on the same restriction fragment, religation is the ligation of juxtaposed fragments, and only valid pairs between two different fragments become contacts. No cut-off is drawn.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nservant/HiC-Pro/master/doc/MANUAL.md
  kind: sankey
  config:
    value_label: Read pairs
  roles:
    steps:
    - mapping
    - filtering
    - contacts

- component: card
  title: Valid pairs by contact class
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of valid read pairs, and the ring splits them by contact class (cis, trans or removed duplicates). The strip gives the smallest and largest single flow. It answers what the surviving pairs are made of.
    How to read: cis contacts join loci on the same chromosome and trans contacts join different chromosomes. A large duplicate share points to a low-complexity library, and a trans share far above the other samples to a noisier one.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nservant/HiC-Pro/master/doc/MANUAL.md
  column: pairs
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: contacts
  filter_expr: col('filtering') == 'Valid pairs'
  caption: valid pairs, by contact class

- component: card
  title: Read pairs by mapping outcome
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of read pairs, and the ring splits them by how they mapped: uniquely mapped, singleton, low quality or unmapped. The strip gives the smallest and largest single flow. It answers how much of the sequencing maps to the genome.
    How to read: a large uniquely mapped share is healthy. Large unmapped or low quality shares point to contamination, poor read quality or the wrong reference.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nservant/HiC-Pro/master/doc/MANUAL.md
  column: pairs
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: mapping
  caption: read pairs, by mapping outcome

- component: table
  title: Read-pair fates table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and a path of mapping outcome, filter outcome and contact class with the number of read pairs that took it. It answers the exact counts behind the flow.
    How to read: filter on a sample and sort by pairs to list its largest fates.

- component: card
  title: Valid-pair funnel
  description: |-
    The hero number is the read pairs sequenced, and the stages below it show how many remain after pairing, the restriction-fragment filter, de-duplication, the cis split and the long-range cut. The strip gives the median and the largest sample. It answers how much of the sequencing ends as useful long-range contacts.
    How to read: each stage should keep a sizeable share of the one before. A sharp drop at the restriction-fragment filter points to the digestion or ligation, and one at de-duplication to a low-complexity library.
    Lines and annotations: long-range contacts are cis pairs more than 20 kb apart and short-range ones are 20 kb apart or less, as HiC-Pro counts them.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nservant/HiC-Pro/master/doc/MANUAL.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nservant/HiC-Pro/master/scripts/merge_valid_interactions.sh
  column: total_pairs
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: attrition
  attrition_cols:
  - reported_pairs
  - valid_pairs
  - valid_pairs_rmdup
  - cis_pairs
  - cis_long_range
  caption: pairs left at each stage

- component: card
  title: Valid pair rate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean share of processed read pairs that are valid pairs, with the lowest and highest sample beside it. It answers how efficient the library is at yielding contacts.
    How to read: a low rate for one sample against the others marks a failed library. Look at the funnel and the read-pair flow to see which step loses the pairs. HiC-Pro defines no cut-off, so judge a sample against its peers.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nservant/HiC-Pro/master/doc/MANUAL.md
  column: valid_pair_rate
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: mean valid pair rate, with its lowest and highest

- component: card
  title: Cis contact share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean share of de-duplicated valid pairs that join loci on the same chromosome, with the lowest and highest sample beside it. It answers how much of the signal is intra-chromosomal.
    How to read: the cis share and the trans share add up to one. A sample whose cis share is far below its peers is noisier, so compare samples because HiC-Pro defines no cut-off.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nservant/HiC-Pro/master/doc/MANUAL.md
  column: cis_ratio
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: mean cis share, with its lowest and highest

- component: card
  title: Long-range share of cis contacts
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean share of cis contacts that are more than 20 kb apart, with the lowest and highest sample beside it. It answers how much of the signal reports distant interactions.
    How to read: long-range cis contacts are the ones a Hi-C run is built to capture, so a low share means the library is dominated by short-range contacts. Compare samples, since HiC-Pro defines no cut-off.
    Lines and annotations: HiC-Pro splits cis contacts into short range (20 kb or less) and long range (over 20 kb).
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nservant/HiC-Pro/master/doc/MANUAL.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nservant/HiC-Pro/master/scripts/merge_valid_interactions.sh
  column: long_range_ratio
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: mean long-range share of cis pairs, with its lowest and highest

- component: card
  title: Duplicate rate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean share of valid pairs removed as duplicates, and the box shows the spread over samples. It answers how redundant the library is.
    How to read: a high rate means the same ligation products were sequenced many times, so the library has low complexity and sequencing deeper adds little. Compare samples to find the outliers.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nservant/HiC-Pro/master/doc/MANUAL.md
  column: duplicate_rate
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: duplicate rate, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Low quality rate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean share of processed read pairs discarded for low mapping quality, and the box shows the spread over samples. It answers how many pairs map ambiguously.
    How to read: a high rate points to repeats, poor read quality or a mismatched reference. Compare samples to find the outliers. The minimum mapping quality is a HiC-Pro setting.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nservant/HiC-Pro/master/doc/MANUAL.md
  column: low_qual_rate
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: low quality rate, with its spread

- component: card
  title: De-duplicated valid pairs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of valid pairs left after de-duplication, with the median, lowest and highest sample beside it. It answers how many usable contacts the run holds.
    How to read: contact maps at fine resolution need many contacts, so a sample with far fewer pairs than its peers limits the resolution you can use.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nservant/HiC-Pro/master/doc/MANUAL.md
  column: valid_pairs_rmdup
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: de-duplicated valid pairs, with their range over samples

- component: card
  title: Long-range cis pairs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of cis pairs more than 20 kb apart, with the median, lowest and highest sample beside it. It answers how many distant contacts the run holds.
    How to read: these are the contacts that carry domain and loop information. A sample far below its peers is a weak one for such analyses.
    Lines and annotations: long range means more than 20 kb between the two ends, as HiC-Pro defines it.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nservant/HiC-Pro/master/doc/MANUAL.md
  column: cis_long_range
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: long-range cis pairs, with their range over samples

- component: card
  title: Trans contact share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean share of de-duplicated valid pairs that join different chromosomes, and the box shows the spread over samples. It answers how much of the signal is inter-chromosomal.
    How to read: it is the complement of the cis share. A sample whose trans share is far above its peers is noisier. HiC-Pro defines no cut-off, so judge a sample against its peers.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nservant/HiC-Pro/master/doc/MANUAL.md
  column: trans_ratio
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: trans share, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Mapping rate of the first mate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean share of first-mate reads that mapped to the genome, and the box shows the spread over samples. It answers how well the reads align before pairing.
    How to read: a low rate points to contamination, poor quality or the wrong reference. HiC-Pro maps reads in two steps and trims reads spanning the ligation junction, so a part of the mapped reads comes from the second step.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nservant/HiC-Pro/master/doc/MANUAL.md
  column: mapping_rate_r1
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: mapping rate, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Valid-pair funnel table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its counts at every stage of the funnel and the rates derived from them. It answers the exact numbers behind each card.
    How to read: sort by valid pair rate to find the weakest libraries, then read the other columns to see which step lost the pairs.
